note: Tier 2, Claims family fast lane. Real Claims, Registry, Core and Rent ELFs with the Product Runtime V3 graph, the LiabilityBasisV2 aggregate, the Core Market and the lifecycle RentCredit INSTALLED directly, so the family routes are reachable with no Hot execution and no open Market. Refusal bindings claim only the entrypoint route unless the campaign observed the handler return; this lane asserts which refusal the chain reported, not which line raised it.

bindings.label: claims position: create lookup table
bindings.note: Address Lookup Table creation. No dClutch program is invoked. The Claims frames are 26 and 15 accounts wide and ride a v0 message over this table.

bindings.label: claims position: extend lookup table *
bindings.note: Address Lookup Table extension, twenty addresses per transaction. No dClutch program is invoked.

bindings.label: claims position: admit under a substituted Position owner
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The admission names a Position owner the caller-authority PDA does not authorize. Refuses Position (0x5145); the campaign asserts the Position account is byte-identical to its prestate.

bindings.label: claims position: admit
bindings.note: The canonical 26-account Admit. Allocates and assigns the runtime-width Position and its admission record, and returns the 512-byte ProtocolPositionAdmissionV2 receipt.

bindings.label: claims position: caller refuses after a complete admission

unnamed_refusal.reason: LiabilityBasisTestCallerError::DeliberateLateFailure (0x102003) -- the Position lifecycle campaign drives its rollback case through the generic forwarding caller at programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/test-programs/liability-basis-caller -- raised AFTER Claims logged success, to prove the allocation and the admission record roll back together. Band 0x102 is that caller's alone and can never appear on a real cluster, so the code no longer collides with any first-party refusal; it is still uncredited because a test caller has no census taxonomy to credit.

bindings.note: The chain's own logs show `Program <claims> success` inside a transaction that did not commit. The campaign asserts the admission account is byte-identical to its prestate.

bindings.label: claims position: admit an already admitted Position
bindings.note: HOSTILE replay. The request declares a Vacant prestate for a Position that now exists. Refuses Position (0x5145).

bindings.label: claims position: close a zero Position
bindings.note: The canonical 15-account Close. Reclaims both the Position and its admission record into the lifecycle RentCredit; the campaign asserts the RentCredit gained exactly the two observed rent principals.

bindings.label: claims position: fund a stranger
bindings.note: The attack itself: one lamport sent from a wallet that is nobody to the keyless, off-curve, system-owned Position PDA. 150 CU, 215 wire bytes, System alone -- no dClutch program is invoked, which is the whole point. Anyone on the network can do this to any pending admission for about one lamport plus a fee.

bindings.label: claims position: an over-declared prepayment is underfunding and still refuses
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the NEGATIVE CONTROL for the relaxation below: an Admit declaring the accounts hold more than they do. Observed once as Custom(20805), caller -> Claims, 155,478 CU. Without this row the front-run row would only prove a guard was removed. Entrypoint route only: the campaign asserts which refusal the chain reported, not which line raised it.

bindings.label: claims position: admission survives a one-lamport front-run
bindings.note: Census row R13, executed: the Admit whose request bytes were fixed BEFORE the stranger's transfer commits anyway, 204,944 CU over four System allocations. The exact-equality balance comparison this replaced made a one-lamport donation a repeatable liveness veto against any pending admission, every slot, forever -- retrying cost strictly more than attacking.

bindings.label: claims position: baseline close sweeps authenticated live donation
bindings.note: The other half of R13: the Close reads the authenticated LIVE balance, so the stranger's lamport lands in the RentCredit with the principal rather than being stranded, burned or unclassified. 99,068 CU, 557 wire bytes.

bindings.label: claims position: close refuses a substituted admission baseline
bindings.note: HOSTILE. A Close presenting an immutable balance baseline other than the one admission recorded. Observed once as Custom(20808), caller -> Claims, 76,419 CU. Entrypoint route only, for the same reason as the over-declared Admit above.

bindings.label: claims sparse: create lookup table
bindings.note: Address Lookup Table creation. No dClutch program is invoked. The composed chain carries 64 account references (1 + 26 + 22 + 15) and cannot ride a legacy message.

bindings.label: claims sparse: extend lookup table *
bindings.note: Address Lookup Table extension, twenty addresses per transaction. No dClutch program is invoked.

bindings.label: claims sparse: transfer of zero
bindings.note: HOSTILE, built as BYTES: the canonical codec refuses a zero quantity at construction, so the only way to put one on the wire is to overwrite the encoded field. Admit returns first and the whole chain rolls back; the campaign asserts the aggregate, both Positions and the RentCredit are byte-identical to their prestate.

bindings.label: claims sparse: transfer under a substituted admission receipt
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The caller carries a receipt that decodes but names another Position owner. This is the check validate_sparse_admission_receipt_v3 owns (commit 78bda05). NOTE: omitting the suffix entirely is NOT refused here -- the adapter treats the receipt as optional and the exact backward dependency is enforced by ClaimsCompositionV3 in the outer controller, which no live route reaches yet.

bindings.label: claims sparse: caller refuses after the complete chain

unnamed_refusal.reason: SparseChainCallerError::DeliberateLateFailure (0x105003), raised by the test-only chain caller at programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/test-programs/sparse-chain-caller AFTER all three Claims stages returned, to prove that a completed three-route composition rolls back whole. Band 0x105 is that caller's alone and can never appear on a real cluster, so the code no longer collides with any first-party refusal; it is still uncredited because a test caller has no census taxonomy to credit.

bindings.note: The strongest rollback case in this tier: three routes, an allocation, an admission record, a liability transfer and a rent reclamation, all undone. The campaign asserts every touched account is byte-identical to its prestate and that the chain's own logs carry three `Program <claims> success` lines inside the failed transaction.

bindings.label: claims sparse: admit, transfer and close
bindings.note: The composition of commit 78bda05, executed: Admit (26 accounts) returns the 512-byte admission receipt, the SparseNativeTransfer (22) consumes it verbatim and returns its 448-byte receipt, and the Close (15) consumes THAT and reclaims the drained source Position. One transaction. The campaign asserts the destination holds exactly the transferred quantity, that the aggregate supply at the moved coordinate is unchanged, and that the RentCredit gained exactly the two observed rent principals.

bindings.label: ordered walk: admit the zero root reserve Position
bindings.note: The prestate the whole retirement walk stands on, and it is BUILT rather than planted: the zero-quantity root reserve Position is admitted through the forwarding caller (204,944 CU, 579 wire bytes, Claims at depth 2 over four System allocations). Nothing downstream of it is installed by the fixture.

bindings.label: ordered walk: begin creates the cursor on a terminal Market
bindings.note: DCFRRQ03 / Begin, and the FIRST census evidence of any kind for `claims/process_begin#Begin`. 41,261 CU, 524 wire bytes, Claims at depth 1 over two System instructions -- the cursor account this walk had none of before. The campaign asserts the receipt settles zero lamports: begin tops a vacant address up to rent exemption and moves no principal.

bindings.label: ordered walk: retire the sole coordinate against real Token-2022
bindings.note: RetireCoordinate against the AUDITED Token-2022 v11 ELF (provenance-checked by the runner), and the first census evidence of any kind for `claims/process_coordinate#RetireCoordinate`. 151,538 CU, 539 wire bytes, caller -> Claims -> Token-2022 at depth 3. The step closes the reserve Position, its admission record and the zero-supply shard Mint, and the campaign asserts all three rent principals land whole in the RentCredit.

bindings.label: ordered walk: finish closes the completed cursor
bindings.note: DCFRRQ03 / Finish, the first census evidence of any kind for `claims/process_finish#Finish`, 32,771 CU, 519 wire bytes, Claims alone in the frame. It closes the cursor and settles its ENTIRE balance -- the rent principal plus the stray lamport a stranger had planted on the address before the walk began -- to the RentCredit. With this row the four-transaction walk -- admit, begin, coordinate, finish -- is executed end to end against real ELFs for the first time, with no planted cursor and no planted intermediate state.

bindings.label: privilege exemption: begin accepts a RentCredit its neighbour writes
bindings.note: The same Begin route with the RentCredit coordinate arriving WRITABLE because a neighbouring instruction in the caller's frame writes it. Begin only reads it, and a route that refused a widened privilege would make the two instructions uncomposable. 41,261 CU -- identical to the read-only frame, which is the point: the privilege is not read.

bindings.label: premature finish: begin the walk
bindings.note: The positive control the hostile below needs. Without it the refusal could be a walk that never began, which is a different fact from a walk that owes a coordinate. 41,261 CU, identical to the ordered walk's begin.

bindings.label: premature finish: a cursor that still owes a coordinate refuses
bindings.note: HOSTILE. A Finish submitted at the revision Begin leaves behind, against a cursor that still owes coordinate 0. Observed once as Custom(20488), Claims alone in the frame, 29,387 CU, and the campaign asserts the refused Finish left the cursor byte-identical to what it found. Entrypoint route only: `ClaimsSbfError::Representation` is one code over many conjuncts, so the chain's own logs do not say which handler raised it, and this tier does not claim a handler it did not observe return.

bindings.label: replay: the first begin
bindings.note: The same Begin against an UNDERFUNDED cursor address, so begin takes the transfer path rather than the top-up path and lands the account on exactly the rent minimum for 296 bytes. 43,061 CU over three System instructions -- 1,800 CU and one instruction more than the over-funded walk, which is the transfer.

bindings.label: replay: the second begin refuses on the cursor's own vacancy
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the anti-replay property has no counter behind it: a second Begin finds the cursor it created and refuses on that account's own existence. Observed once as Custom(20488), Claims alone, 33,238 CU, and the campaign asserts the refused begin left the created cursor byte-identical. Entrypoint route only, for the same reason as the premature Finish above.

bindings.label: claims fractional retirement: admit zero root Position
bindings.note: The rollback campaign's prestate: the same 204,944-CU Admit, on the fixture whose Token program is a refusing stand-in rather than Token-2022.

bindings.label: claims fractional retirement: canonical Token program refuses at late Mint close CPI

unnamed_refusal.reason: LiabilityBasisTestCallerError::Instruction (0x102000) -- NOT a Token-2022 refusal. The stand-in installed at the canonical Token-2022 address for this campaign is programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/test-programs/liability-basis-caller, which refuses every instruction it does not recognise. Band 0x102 is that caller's alone and can never appear on a real cluster; it is uncredited because a test caller has no census taxonomy to credit.

bindings.note: HOSTILE, and it is the retirement coordinate's atomicity: the CampaignV1::LateTokenRefusal fixture installs the test caller ELF AT THE CANONICAL TOKEN-2022 ADDRESS, so RetireCoordinate authenticates its whole frame, closes what it closes and then hits a Token program that refuses everything. 147,713 CU, 539 wire bytes. The campaign asserts the Position, the admission, the RentCredit, the cursor and the shard Mint are each byte-identical to their prestate. The coordinate route is claimed here and not merely the entrypoint, because the transaction's own logs carry `Program <Token-2022 canonical id> invoke [3]` inside a Claims frame, the campaign asserts that line by name, and `process_coordinate` is the only Claims route that CPIs the Token program to close a shard Mint.
